rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF THE AMOUNT OF THREE BILLION EIGHT HUNDRED FIFTY MILLION PESOS (P3,850,000,000 .00) TO SUPPORT THE ADJUSTMENTS OF THE PENSION RATES OF WIDOWS, RETIRED OFFICERS AND MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES(AFP) EFFECTIVE DECEMBER 1, 1987 BASED ON THE NEW RATES OF PAY FOR MILITARY PERSONNEL, AS PROVIDED FOR IN PRESIDENTIAL DECREES NUMBERED 1638 AND 1909 AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6638
rows.abstract: "AFP Supplementary Act of 2000". Rationale: The budgetary allocation for the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) as stipulated in the General Appropriations Act (GAA) for the Fiscal Years 1987 to 1992 fails to include as part of expenditure the adjustment of pension rates of retired AFP military personnel. Republic Act 6638 mandates that the pension rates of retired AFP military personnel should be based on the prevailing rates of compensation for military personnel who are in active service.Given the aforementioned, widespread demoralization and frstration haunts AFP retirees and their beneficiaries. Deprivation of what is due after risking life and limb, and after sacrificing time, sweat and blood, clearly degrades not only integritybut also life's meaning itself.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Times and experience have proven the competence and capability of the Junior Geodetic Engineers in performing their tasks. rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING TO USE THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE AS THE MEDIUM OF COMMUNICATION IN ALL GOVERNMENT-SPON SORED EXAMINATIONS
rows.abstract: Rationale: The government-spon sored examinations, such as the National Elementary Aptitude Test for the elementary pupils; the National Secondary Aptitude Test for the high school students; the Civil Service examination for the government-woul d-beemployees and the licensure examinations for teachers, have questions in the Tagalog dialect.  > Understandably, the students and examinees who study in the non-Tagalog speaking provinces, are placed in a disadvantageous position because of their deficiency in the Tagalog dialect. Thus, as to level the playing field , it is heeby proposed that all government-spon sored examinations should use the English language as the medium of communication.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 289, paragraph 6 of Republic Act No. 8424 needs to be amended for its effective implementation by providing that the share of the beneficiary provinces equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the excise taxes on locally manufactured Virginia-type cigarettes be directly allocated to them. > The beneficiary provinces are in a better position to ensure that the said fund shall be used for priority cooperative projects, livelihood projects, agro-industrial projects such as farm-to-market roads.

rows.author: A073
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6938, ENTITLED `AN ACT TO ORDAIN A COOPERATIVES CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES,' WHICH IS KNOWN AS THE `COOPERATIVES CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES,' PROVIDING THE MECHANISM FOR THEIR IMPLEMENTATION, AND FOROTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to encourage the formation of more prinary cooepratives, especially among our countryside farmers and small fishermen, by reducing the initial organizational membership requirement to a minimum of only seven (7) well-acquainted organizers for the first two (2) years and affording the organizers enough experience and time to select additional cooperators to complete the minimum required number of fifteen (15) members by the 1st Quarter of the 3rd Year from the date of registration of the cooperative.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT (SPECIAL CTTE.) since 1999-10-08
